title: Stack Buffer Overflow in cURL wolfSSL Backend (lib/vtls/wolfssl.c)
classified_slop_by: Daniel Stenberg gist 07f7581f6e3d78ef37dfbfc81fd1d1cd (AI slop security reports submitted to curl)
why_rejected: Closed on HackerOne as not-applicable and listed as AI slop in Stenberg's gist. The claim is bogus: the PoC never calls libcurl — it reimplements a strcpy-into-a-12-byte-buffer pattern in a standalone program and ASan flags that program's own overflow. In the real wssl_strerror the source strings are curl's own fixed, bounded literals copied into an adequately sized caller buffer, not attacker-controlled data, so no runtime overflow exists even with DEBUGASSERT compiled out. No crash is demonstrated against curl. The public disclosure JSON exposes no maintainer comment text.
note: report.md is the reporter's description with PoC source and raw AddressSanitizer output removed; it is framed as the reporter's claims.
